name: Nauru
summary_text: Nauru demands real caution. Same-sex conduct decriminalised in 2016; tiny population (~12,000); no LGR; no documented anti-trans violence; the asylum-detention legacy shaped its international image but not its LGBT law. Caveat: very small population — the evidence base is thin, so this assessment carries greater-than-usual uncertainty.

sources.claim_summary: ILGA World Database jurisdiction page for Nauru: documents the legal status — same-sex conduct decriminalised in 2016.

sources.title: Human Dignity Trust
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Only the Human Dignity Trust homepage was retrievable at fetch time (no Nauru-specific page); Nauru decriminalised same-sex conduct in 2016.

sources.title: Over 80 Nations Support Statement at Human Rights Council on LGBT Rights - U.S. Mission to International Organizations in Geneva
sources.claim_summary: US Mission in Geneva (March 2011): post on LGBT rights in the UN context - US diplomatic advocacy for SOGI rights at the Human Rights Council; Nauru was among Pacific countries supporting the call.

sources.title: LGBT Rights Across the World: Which are the Best and Worst Countries?
sources.claim_summary: Human Truth Foundation 'LGBT Rights Across the World' (Vexen Crabtree, 2025): the Vexen LGBT Equality Index ranking all countries (Germany/Spain top at 4.88; Saudi Arabia bottom at -11.30) - comparative index covering Nauru.

sources.title: Nauru decriminalises homosexuality and suicide | Nauru | The Guardian
sources.claim_summary: The Guardian (May 2016): Nauru decriminalised homosexuality and attempted suicide - new laws replaced the 1899 Queensland-based criminal code, following a spate of suicide attempts by refugees on the island.

sources.title: Nauru - Kaleidoscope Trust
sources.claim_summary: Kaleidoscope Trust Nauru page: Nauru decriminalised consensual same-sex conduct in 2016, but same-sex marriage/unions remain illegal; no explicit legal recognition or protection for intersex and trans people; no employment-discrimination protection; supported the 2011 UN Joint Statement on SOGI; CEDAW Committee categorised as 'No Recognition of LBTI Rights'.
